# Synthetic StuffIt fixtures

Every archive here is synthetic: all fork contents are generated (hand-written sentences, word-list text, counters, runs, xorshift pseudo-random bytes, zero-length forks, and the short strings printed in the specification's worked examples) and no byte comes from a real archive or file. Each archive was listed, tested and extracted with `unar`/`lsar` 1.10.7, and every fork `unar` extracts equals the generated bytes. The generators are deliberately not part of this repository. One exception to "tested": `lsar -t` reports "Unpacking failed" for the zero-length data fork that carries method 13 in `sit5-m13-empty.sit` and in entry 10 of `sit5-m13-tree.sit` (crate-written; genuine archives give empty forks method 0), while `unar` extracts it as an empty file. The expected result is an empty fork: a fork of unpacked length 0 is never decoded.

The archives come from two generations of tooling:

- **Crate-written set** (methods 0, 1, 2, 3 and predefined-set-1 method 13). StuffIt 5 archives were written by the `stuffit` crate, version 0.1.8, used as a black box through its public API; classic `SIT!` archives were assembled by hand (22-byte archive header, 112-byte record headers) around packed forks obtained from that crate (method 13), from `compress -b 14` with its 3-byte header removed (method 2), or from minimal encoders written for this purpose (methods 1 and 3). Two things were changed after the crate wrote the StuffIt 5 archives. (1) The header checksums were corrected, because genuine StuffIt 5 archives differ from the crate's output: the entry header checksum is the CRC-16 of the whole entry header with the checksum field taken as zero, and the file header checksum at offset 98 is the CRC-16 of bytes 0..113 (both ends included) with the field taken as zero, followed by `0D A5 A5 "Reserved" A5 A5 00`. (2) The names were rewritten as MacRoman bytes on purpose. That is not how genuine StuffIt 5 archives store names: every non-ASCII name found in real StuffIt 5 archives (38 of 38) is UTF-8, which is also what the crate writes. The specification's rule for StuffIt 5 names (`docs/stuffit/containers.md` section 2.6) is: every byte below 0x80 means ASCII; otherwise well-formed UTF-8 means UTF-8; otherwise MacRoman. These archives store MacRoman so that the last branch, which no real archive on hand exercises, is covered; none of their non-ASCII names is well-formed UTF-8, so the rule decodes each to the name in the manifest. The UTF-8 branch is covered by `nonstandard/sit5-m0-names-utf8-as-written.sit`. The second-block checksum of these archives is zero, which is not what genuine archives carry (a finding, not an error, for a non-strict reader). Unmodified crate output is kept only under `nonstandard/`.
- **Specification-written set** (method 15, and method 13 in every table mode): the files `*-m15-*`, `*-m13-vectors.sit`, `*-m13-predefined.sit` and `*-m13-dynamic.sit`. Containers were assembled byte by byte from `docs/stuffit/containers.md`, with all three StuffIt 5 header checksums (file header, entry header, second block) and all classic header checksums correct. The packed streams are either the hex streams printed in `docs/stuffit/arsenic.md` and `docs/stuffit/lz-methods.md`, wrapped unchanged, or the output of encoders written from those two documents. Fork checksum fields hold the CRC-16 of the unpacked fork, except method 15 forks in StuffIt 5 archives, which hold `0000` as genuine archives do.

## Directories

| Directory | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `.` | Valid archives. `unar` extracts every fork to the generated bytes; the `ref_*` columns of the manifest and the `expect_*` columns of `forks.tsv` are the conformance target. |
| `nonstandard/` | Unmodified crate output that deviates from genuine StuffIt 5 but that `docs/stuffit/containers.md` (section 4.11) says a tolerant reader must still accept. Expected results are listed below. |

Crate 0.1.8 does not decode every fork of the main set correctly. The crate-derived manifest columns record what it actually returned; they are known wrong for:

| Archive | Entries | What the crate does |
|---|---|---|
| `classic-m1-runs.sit`, `classic-m1-rsrc-only.sit`, `classic-m1-both-forks.sit`, `classic-m1-names.sit`, `classic-m1-tree.sit` | every method 1 fork that contains a run | wrong bytes (status `ok` or `short`) |
| `classic-m13-vectors.sit`, `sit5-m13-vectors.sit` | 5 (`V06 set 4`) | wrong bytes with status `ok` |
| `classic-m13-predefined.sit`, `sit5-m13-predefined.sit` | 3 (`predefined set 4`) | status `short` |
| `classic-m15-both-forks.sit` | 0, both forks | no decoder for method 15 in the classic container: status `error` |

## Files

`sit5-mN-*` exist for N = 0, 13, 15. `classic-mN-*` exist for N = 0, 1, 2, 3, 13, 15.

| File pattern | Covers |
|---|---|
| `*-empty.sit` | One file, both forks zero length. In classic archives empty forks carry method 0. |
| `*-onebyte.sit` | One file, 1-byte data fork (`41`). |
| `*-text.sit` | One file, 547 bytes of CR-terminated text, data fork only. |
| `*-runs.sit` | One file, 3616 bytes of runs: runs longer than 255, a single `90` byte, nine `90` bytes, `abc` repeated, short runs of 1..7. |
| `*-random.sit` | One file, 2000 incompressible pseudo-random bytes. |
| `*-rsrc-only.sit` | One file, resource fork only (1604 bytes; arbitrary bytes, not a valid resource map). |
| `*-both-forks.sit` | One file with a data fork (547) and a resource fork (1611). |
| `*-tree.sit` | 14 entries: folders nested 4 deep, an empty folder, four sibling files next to a subfolder, a file after a subfolder, two root entries, eight distinct type/creator pairs, files with data only, resource only, both and neither. |
| `*-names.sit` | Names with non-ASCII characters, stored as MacRoman bytes in both container generations (for StuffIt 5 this exercises the MacRoman fallback of the name rule; see above) (`Résumé – naïve café.txt`, `Ærøskøbing ƒ ∆ π ™`, folder `Dossier été`, `Übergröße©.dat`), a creator code with a high byte (`86 6E 72 74`), a name containing `:` and, as the last entry, a root-level name containing `/` (`slash/inside`). The manifest path keeps that `/` verbatim, so it is indistinguishable from a separator there. |
| `sit5-m13-large.sit`, `classic-m13-large.sit` | One 100000-byte text file, larger than the method 13 window. |
| `classic-m2-table-reset.sit` | One 115000-byte file whose LZW stream reaches 14-bit codes, fills the table and contains one clear code. |

Terms in this file follow `docs/stuffit/README.md` (glossary): packed and unpacked bytes and lengths, fork checksum, record header (classic), entry header and file header (StuffIt 5), CRC-16 as defined in `docs/stuffit/containers.md` section 2.1. The manifest column names (`*_declared_len`, `crc16`) are kept as they are: "declared length" there is the unpacked length U, and `crc16` is the fork checksum field.

Classic container details chosen by hand: archive header `SIT!`, top-level record count, total length, `rLau`, version 2, zero, header length 22, two zero bytes; folders are a folder start marker (both method bytes `20`) and a folder end marker (both `21`) with zero lengths; bytes 34..35 of each record header hold the name checksum (CRC-16 of bytes 2..33), bytes 36..65 are zero (the specification-written set fills the sibling offsets at 50..57), dates are fixed, each fork checksum is the CRC-16 of the unpacked fork, bytes 110..111 hold the header checksum (CRC-16 of bytes 0..109).

### Method 15 (Arsenic)

All entries are files at the root with ASCII names. Section and vector numbers refer to `docs/stuffit/arsenic.md`.

`sit5-m15-vectors.sit`: the printed streams, one per entry, data fork only.

| Entry | Name | Stream | Covers |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 0 | `s13 worked example` | section 13.2 | The fully traced stream; block-size field 0; one repeat count. |
| 1 | `P01 no blocks` | P1 | Zero-block stream. The fork has unpacked length 0 and packed length 8, so a container reader delivers an empty fork without decoding; its 8 packed bytes still occupy their place before the next entry. Decoded as a stream with expected length 0 it yields empty output. |
| 2 | `P02 zero run at start` | P2 | Zero run at the start of a block; repeat count. |
| 3 | `P03 two blocks` | P3 | Two blocks; model reset and fresh move-to-front list. |
| 4 | `P04 count dropped mid` | P4 | A block that is not the last ends with the repeat counter at 4. |
| 5 | `P05 count dropped end` | P5 | The last block ends with the repeat counter at 4. |
| 6 | `P06 counter not carried` | P6 | Repeat counter restarts at a block boundary. |
| 7 | `P07 randomised block` | P7 | Randomised block with one flip (position 238); count bytes of 0. |
| 8 | `P08 block at capacity` | P8 | Block length equal to the block capacity (512). |
| 9 | `P09 class fallback` | P9 | Last-symbol fallback in the class model. |
| 10 | `P10 primary fallback` | P10 | The same fallback twice in the primary model; every bit of the last byte is requested. |
| 11 | `P11 fourteen blocks` | P11 | Block-size field 10, 14 blocks, three randomised blocks (flip table used past its end; a flagged block too short to flip; restart per block), class, rank 1 and primary model halving, every class symbol and rank model, run expansion with counts 0, 1 and 255. |
| 12 | `T01 trailing bytes` | section 13.2 stream followed by 5 pseudo-random bytes | Bytes after the end of the stream are ignored (section 11.3). |

`sit5-m15-blocksizes.sit`: 16 entries, `block size field 00` to `block size field 15`, each a different 2000 to 2555 byte text encoded with that block-size field (origin index 9 to 24 bits wide). Field 0 gives 4 blocks, fields 1 and 2 give 2 blocks, the others 1.

`sit5-m15-large.sit`: one file, both forks method 15 with block-size field 10.

| Fork | Unpacked | Packed | Blocks | Covers |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| data | 400000 | 82292 | 13 (8492 to 65537 packed bytes each) | Word-list text with 16 inserted runs of 3 to 4000 equal bytes (lengths around 4, 259, 263 and 518, where the run-length stage changes shape). Blocks 3, 4 and 8 (counting from 1) are randomised, with 503, 65 and 512 flips. The primary model is halved once (more than 255 header and framing symbols); class and rank 1 to rank 4 models are halved. |
| rsrc | 60000 | 37040 | 2 | Structured binary (runs, counters, skewed and uniform pseudo-random bytes; not a valid resource map). Block 1 is randomised (140 flips). Every model except the primary is halved, including rank 5, rank 6 and rank 7, which no printed vector reaches. |

`classic-m15-both-forks.sit`: one file in the classic container with both forks method 15 (data 787 bytes in 2 blocks, resource 1604 bytes), block-size field 10. Fork checksum fields hold the CRC-16 of the unpacked fork. No genuine classic archive uses method 15; the specification selects the decoder by method number alone, and `unar` extracts this archive.

### Method 13

Section numbers refer to `docs/stuffit/lz-methods.md`. Each of the following exists as `classic-…` and `sit5-…` with identical entries and identical packed streams.

`*-m13-vectors.sit`: the printed streams, one per entry, data fork only.

| Entry | Name | Stream | Header byte | Unpacked |
|--:|---|---|---|--:|
| 0 | `V01 set 1 worked example` | section 6.10 | `11` | 10 |
| 1 | `V02 set 1 real padding` | 6.10 variant with zero padding to a multiple of 4 bytes after the header | `11` | 10 |
| 2 | `V03 dynamic shared` | section 6.11: shared code, 10 distance symbols, absent symbols with value 0 and -1 | `08` | 7 |
| 3 | `V04 set 2` | 6.12 | `23` | 19 |
| 4 | `V05 set 3` | 6.12 | `34` | 19 |
| 5 | `V06 set 4` | 6.12 | `41` | 19 |
| 6 | `V07 set 5` | 6.12 | `51` | 19 |
| 7 | `V08 length symbol 318` | 6.12: 10-bit length field | `11` | 101 |
| 8 | `V09 length symbol 319` | 6.12: 15-bit length field | `11` | 1103 |
| 9 | `V10 set 3 distance bits` | 6.12: distance symbol with a 4-bit field | `34` | 41 |
| 10 | `V11 dynamic separate` | 6.12: separate secondary code; current length restarts per description; a match read with the secondary code | `00` | 12 |
| 11 | `V12 end code secondary` | 6.12: output complete directly before an end-of-data symbol in the secondary code | `00` | 4 |
| 12 | `V13 low header bits ignored` | 6.10 variant | `1F` | 10 |
| 13 | `V14 padding bit set` | 6.10 variant | `11` | 10 |
| 14 | `V15 no end code` | 6.10 variant: no end-of-data codeword after the last item | `11` | 10 |
| 15 | `V16 match cut by length` | 6.10 stream with unpacked length 7: the match is cut short | `11` | 7 |

`*-m13-predefined.sit`: five entries `predefined set 1` to `predefined set 5`, word-list text (900, 2900, 6100, 1000 and 800 bytes) encoded with that table set and laid out as real encoders do (header low bits = distance alphabet size minus 10, end-of-data codeword, zero padding to a multiple of 4 bytes after the header). Each text ends with a copy of its first 48 bytes, so the largest distance symbol of the set is used; all five contain a run coded with length symbol 318, sets 2 and 3 also a repeated pair coded with symbol 319. Set 3 uses all 14 distance symbols.

`*-m13-dynamic.sit`: sixteen entries `dynamic header 00` to `dynamic header 0F`, one per dynamic header value (`00` to `07` separate secondary code, `08` to `0F` shared; 10 to 17 distance symbols). Data forks are word-list text of 552, 1092, 2092, 4192, 8292, 16492, 32992 and 65992 bytes for 10 to 17 distance symbols; each uses the largest distance symbol of its alphabet (largest distance 61797, in `0F`). Entries `06` and `0E` also have a resource fork (30000 and 3000 bytes of structured binary) with the same header value. Code lengths reach 13 bits; the table descriptions use the set-length commands for lengths 2 to 13 and all of mark-absent, one-longer, one-shorter and the three repeat commands; they take 408 to 1632 bits. Length symbols 318 and 319 occur from 12 and 14 distance symbols upwards. All codes are complete, absent symbols are always introduced by the mark-absent command, and every stream ends with the end-of-data codeword and zero padding to a multiple of 4 bytes after the header.

### `nonstandard/`

Crate output untouched. All three deviate from genuine StuffIt 5 in the same ways: the file header checksum at offset 98 and the 14 bytes after it are wrong, every entry header checksum is wrong, every second-block checksum is zero, there are no end-of-folder markers, and a first child's previous offset is 0. Fork data and fork checksums are correct.

| File | Expected result from a tolerant (non-strict) reader |
|---|---|
| `nonstandard/sit5-m0-text-as-written.sit` | Accepted. One file `short text.txt`, method 0 data fork of 547 bytes extracted with a matching fork checksum. Findings only: file header, entry header and second-block checksum mismatches. |
| `nonstandard/sit5-m13-text-as-written.sit` | The same with a method 13 data fork (364 packed bytes). |
| `nonstandard/sit5-m0-names-utf8-as-written.sit` | Accepted, complete listing of 5 entries: two root files, folder `Dossier été` and its two files (the folder's chain ends with a next offset of 0 after the 2 children its count announces). Names are stored as UTF-8 and are decoded as UTF-8 by the StuffIt 5 name rule, giving exactly the names in `name_hex`. All forks extract with matching fork checksums. The same checksum findings. |

Under strict checksum checking all three are rejected as not StuffIt 5 (file header checksum mismatch). The manifest rows of these archives carry the expected names, lengths and hashes (`ref_*`), which `unar` reproduces.

The crate's method 14 and method 15 output was removed: its method 15 streams are not valid Arsenic (no checksum, no run-length stage) and `unar` cannot read its method 14 forks.

### Not covered

- Method 14 in either container; classic methods 5, 6 and 8; StuffIt 5 forks with methods 1, 2 or 3.
- Encryption, segmented archives, MacBinary-wrapped or embedded archives, entry comments.
- StuffIt 5 folders in the genuine shape (end-of-folder markers, leading and trailing layout, empty folders) and StuffIt 5 names stored as UTF-8 in an otherwise genuine archive. The `sit5-*-tree.sit` and `sit5-*-names.sit` archives have crate-style folders without markers.
- Archives or streams that must be rejected. The rejection vectors of `arsenic.md` (R1 to R12) and the error rows of `lz-methods.md` exist only as printed hex in those documents.
- Method 13: incomplete codes, absent symbols with values other than -1 outside `V03`, code lengths above 13 bits, table-description set-length commands for lengths 1 and 14 to 31 outside the vectors.
- Method 15: a block-size field other than 10 combined with more than 4 blocks; blocks longer than 65537 bytes.

## manifest.tsv

UTF-8, tab separated, one header row, rows sorted by `archive` (byte order) then `entry_index`.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `archive` | Archive path relative to this directory. |
| `format` | `classic` or `sit5`. |
| `entry_index` | 0-based position in archive order, folders included. |
| `name_hex` | Lowercase hex of the UTF-8 bytes of the full path, components joined with `/`. This is the intended name and the one the specification's decode rule gives (MacRoman for classic; ASCII, else well-formed UTF-8, else MacRoman for StuffIt 5). Crate 0.1.8 returns U+FFFD for the MacRoman bytes of the main-set StuffIt 5 names because it decodes StuffIt 5 names as UTF-8 only. The path is the plain join of the decoded names, without the safe-component steps of `docs/stuffit/containers.md` section 2.6. |
| `is_folder` | 0 or 1. Folders have 0 / empty fork columns. |
| `type_hex`, `creator_hex` | The 4-byte type and creator codes, 8 hex digits each. |
| `data_method`, `rsrc_method` | Compression method number with flag bits masked off. |
| `data_packed_len`, `rsrc_packed_len` | Packed length from the entry header. |
| `data_declared_len`, `rsrc_declared_len` | Unpacked length from the entry header. |
| `data_status`, `rsrc_status` | Result of decoding with the crate: `ok` (exactly the declared length), `short` (fewer bytes), `error` (decoder failed, or the crate has no decoder for the method in that container), `none` (fork absent or zero unpacked length). `ok` does not imply correct bytes; see the table of known crate errors above. |
| `data_len`, `data_fnv64`, `rsrc_len`, `rsrc_fnv64` | Length and FNV-1a 64 hash of the bytes the crate decoded; empty for `error` and `none`. |
| `ref_data_len`, `ref_data_fnv64`, `ref_rsrc_len`, `ref_rsrc_fnv64` | The same for the fork as extracted by `unar`; empty when the fork is absent. These are the expected results. For the specification-written set they were also compared byte for byte with the generated content. |

Every present fork of every archive has `ref_*` values. Where the crate columns differ from them, the crate is wrong.

FNV-1a 64-bit: offset basis `0xcbf29ce484222325`, prime `0x100000001b3`, per byte `h = (h XOR byte) * prime mod 2^64`, printed as 16 lowercase hex digits.

## forks.tsv

UTF-8, tab separated, one header row, one row per fork whose packed or unpacked length is not zero, for every archive of the manifest, in manifest order (`data` before `rsrc` within an entry).

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `archive`, `entry_index` | As in the manifest. |
| `fork` | `data` or `rsrc`. |
| `method` | Compression method number. |
| `offset` | Byte offset of the fork's first packed byte within the archive file. |
| `packed_len`, `unpacked_len` | Lengths from the entry header. |
| `crc16` | Fork checksum field of the entry header, 4 lowercase hex digits (`0000` for method 15 forks in StuffIt 5 archives). |
| `expect_len`, `expect_fnv64` | Length and FNV-1a 64 hash of the unpacked fork (the manifest's `ref_*` values). |

Offsets were computed by a parser written from `docs/stuffit/containers.md` and agree with the offsets `lsar` reports for the specification-written set. Every row was validated: the bytes at `offset .. offset + packed_len`, decoded on their own with the row's method and unpacked length, give `expect_len` and `expect_fnv64` (decoded by the crate for 263 rows; for the 12 rows the crate gets wrong, re-wrapped in a one-entry archive and extracted by `unar`). The one row with unpacked length 0 (`sit5-m15-vectors.sit`, entry 1) expects empty output.
